newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel breaks 3.31 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel breaks 3.31 per dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel fell to a new all-time low against the dollar on Tuesday, propelled downwards by the U.S. currency's rise on overseas markets.
Dealers said investors remained indifferent to the Bank of Israel's decision on Monday to reduce its key lending rate by 0.5 points to 14.2 percent.

"The rate cut had no impact on trading today. The shekel continued to decline and the central bank had to intervene again (buying dollars) to support the basket," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.

"The main reason for the shekel's decline was that the dollar rose abroad to a new high against the mark. The only thing that can prevent the shekel from falling further is a decision to change the diagonal rate and the trading band," she said.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

Israel's biggest daily newspaper, Yedioth Ahronoth, said on Tuesday the Bank of Israel proposed cancelling the arrangement and allowing the rate to be set by free trade in the foreign currency market. The Bank of Israel denied the report.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3190 shekels against 3.3060 shekels on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6253 shekels against 3.6247 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7466 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7695 on Monday and against the mark at 2.0062 shekels against 2.0175 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3140 shekels.
